top_story_title: Ivanti Connect Secure: three chained zero-days, root on fully patched appliances, CVE-2026-104935 in KEV with a 16 October deadline
top_story_summary: Ivanti published an advisory on 13 October 2026 for CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290) in Ivanti Connect Secure carrying a CVSSv3.0 score of 8.6 and allowing a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands. Ivanti states that exploitation in the wild occurred before disclosure, affecting a limited number of customers - this was a zero-day. CISA confirmed exploitation and added the CVE to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day, with a remediation due date of 16 October 2026 and ransomware use listed as unknown.
top_actions: Inventory every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance with its exact running version today; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and apply it in an emergency window, not the next routine cycle.
Run the Ivanti Integrity Checker Tool and preserve its output before and after the upgrade; a clean post-upgrade result does not clear a pre-upgrade compromise.

Assume credential and configuration theft: terminate all active VPN sessions, revoke session tokens, and rotate local admin credentials, service accounts, certificates and any secrets stored on or reachable from the appliance.
Treat the third, still-unfixed flaw as live exposure - restrict the administrative interface to a management network or jump host, and apply geo/ASN conditional access on the user-facing portal.

Hunt now rather than after the change window: review /var logs for unusual timestamps, look for new or modified local accounts, altered web resources, and unexpected outbound connections from the appliance.
executive_summary: An unknown actor, UTA0576, chained three Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days to unauthenticated root command execution on an appliance that was fully patched at the time (22.8R2.4); CVE-2026-104935 is in CISA KEV with a 16 October 2026 due date.

Two of the three Ivanti flaws now have fixes and a third is still pending per Volexity, so patching is necessary but not sufficient - rotate credentials, certificates and session tokens and hunt for prior access.

Citrix, Fortinet and Ivanti collectively patched 29 vulnerabilities, including critical authentication bypass, code execution and authentication-information-leak flaws; pull the per-vendor advisories and match them to your running versions.

Cisco disclosed a UEFI Shell Secure Boot bypass on UCS servers and UCS-based appliances, exploitable by an admin-role account or anyone with physical access - relevant if your management or security appliances run on UCS.

Check Point Research found two high-risk flaws in the LiteLLM LLM gateway, including read-only-to-admin takeover: AI infrastructure is inside the perimeter and often outside the appliance patch cycle.
Four items in this window concerned an arrest at OpenAI over a hidden recording device and are not network infrastructure news; they are dropped.
key_actions: **Ivanti** — Confirm the running version on every Connect Secure appliance against the vendor's fixed-release table; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and schedule an emergency upgrade.
**Ivanti** — Run the Ivanti Integrity Checker Tool and keep the output as evidence; run it again after the upgrade.
**Ivanti** — Patch to the vendor's fixed build and run the vendor Integrity Checker Tool.
**Ivanti** — Treat any appliance that was internet-facing in early October 2026 as in scope for investigation regardless of its patch level at the time.
**Ivanti** — Raise an emergency change for the Connect Secure estate today; upgrade the HA secondary first, then fail over and complete the pair.
**Ivanti** — Check the vendor advisory for the fixed release before building the change - do not assume a version from press coverage.
**Ivanti** — Scope the investigation by exposure window, not by patch level: any internet-facing Connect Secure appliance during the first week of October 2026 onward is in scope.
**Ivanti** — Rotate everything the configuration contained: LDAP/AD bind accounts, RADIUS and TACACS+ shared secrets, certificates, API keys and VPN pre-shared keys.

ai_defenses.what_it_does: Cisco describes CSDL evolving to support AI-driven development, with the stated goal of secure and resilient software at speed. The source is a vendor description of its approach, not a product launch.

headlines.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-104935)
headlines.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass in Connect Secure already exploited as a zero-day, and CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 16 October due date.

headlines.title: Ivanti Zero-Day Chain Gave Attackers Root Access to Fully Patched VPN
headlines.summary: A zero-day chain gave attackers unauthenticated remote code execution with elevated privileges on Ivanti Connect Secure appliances that were fully patched at the time.

headlines.title: Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: Ivanti urged Connect Secure customers to patch immediately after confirming active zero-day exploitation of the remote access gateway.

headlines.title: Attackers chained three Ivanti zero-days to gain root on fully patched VPN appliances
headlines.summary: Volexity attributes the Ivanti Connect Secure intrusions to UTA0576, which reached root on a fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance and exfiltrated credentials and configuration data.

headlines.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
headlines.summary: Two of the three Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days used in the attack chain now have fixes; per Volexity a fix for the third is still pending.

headlines.title: Citrix, Fortinet, Ivanti Patch 29 Vulnerabilities Across Their Products
headlines.summary: Citrix, Fortinet and Ivanti shipped fixes for 29 vulnerabilities, including critical authentication bypass, code execution and authentication-information-leak flaws.
